criticalScopeNotes: Critical flags follow the prospective case-specific criticalIf patterns. Wrong/off-target replies are F even when they do not assert the specifically annotated critical proposition.

r01-o1-w0 and r02-o0-w0 assert a false color for the other object, while omitting the requested object; they are F, with critical=false under the narrow requested-object color pattern. This boundary should remain visible beside any primary disagreement.
Known-location denials in r03/r04 are F, but do not assign an alternative location from the narrow criticalIf; critical=false does not mean factually correct.
An off-target recital of another given loan (r08-o1-w1) is F; no false umbrella loan is inferred from the magazine statement. Broken fragments do not become invented facts by reconstruction.
partialBoundaryNotes: r05-o0-w0/w1 and r06-o1-w1 preserve the correct kinship/neighborhood fragment but omit the explicitly requested proper name: P, never C.
r07-o1-w1 gives «a Silvia» as a useful correct recipient, but the stray verb prevents an unequivocally complete relation: P.
h02 turn1 in both branches partly preserves known yellow and missing who, but does not clearly distinguish the uninformed manufacturer: P.
h01 ideal turn3 is C: the interposed «guas» does not obscure the correct complete owner relation. Valid meaning is not penalized for failing exact match.
interpretation: Only one of48 single-turn cells is C; it occurs for the cup under reversed fact order and paraphrased question. This is local wording/order sensitivity in this small DEV sample, not universal linguistic invariance.

Ideal history adds one C at h02 turn2 (Mateo) versus actual history; both branches remain incomplete in all four dialogs. This diagnostic aid does not establish unassisted conversational success or isolate a single cause.
Intelligibility scores are optional descriptive0–3 only. Fluent but wrong/missing answers retain F; no aggregate B score or fluency acceptance threshold is introduced.
